title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). An automorphism u of the profinite group π̂_{0,3} (free profinite on two generators; Galois–Teichmüller / 'équation des lacets' context) determines an element f ∈ π̂_{0,3}, well defined up to f ↦ l_0^n f. Its image in SL(2,Ẑ)/±1 is a matrix (r s; t u) with ru − st = 1. Since left multiplication by l_0^n = (1 −2n; 0 1) changes only the top row, the bottom row (t,u) is determined up to sign by u. The same holds for α_0 = (a b; c d) and its bottom row (c,d). μ ∈ Ẑ* is the multiplier (cyclotomic-type character) with 2ν = μ − 1. ε_2, ε_3 ∈ {±1} are signs attached to the order-2 and order-3 relations.

Two matrix embeddings are in play:
- ρ = (0 1; −1 1), with ρ² − ρ + 1 = 0, so cρ + d = (d c; −c c+d), of determinant c² + cd + d² (Eisenstein integers).
- σ_∞ = (0 1; −1 0), so tσ_∞ + u = (u t; −t u), of determinant t² + u² (Gaussian integers).

On this page Grothendieck conjectures relation (80): ū =? μ α(cρ+d) = μ f^{-1} l_0^{-ν} α_0 (cρ+d), where α = f^{-1} l_0^{-ν} α_0 and ū = μ(u ε_2t; −t ε_2u) is the canonical matrix of (75). He expects it at least when ε_2 = 1, and adds a marginal NB that it holds only up to the sign δ = ε_3 (cf. (82)).

Verification.
1. (a b; c d)(d c; −c c+d) = (ad−bc, ac+bc+bd; 0, c²+cd+d²) =: δ(1 B; 0 D), with δ = ad − bc = ±1.
2. Left-multiplying by (1 2ν; 0 1) gives (81): l_0^{-ν}α_0(cρ+d) = δ(1 C; 0 D), with C = B + 2νD.
3. Then μα(cρ+d) = μδ (u −s; −t r)(1 C; 0 D) = μδ(u, uC − sD; −t, −tC + rD), which he rewrites as δ(μu, −s + μuC; −μt, r − μtC).
4. Using C = ε_2T = ε_2(rt+su) from (61) and the norm relation ε_2μ(t²+u²) = 1, he gets −s + μuC = ε_2μt(ru − st) = ε_2μt.
5. The next page gives r − μtC = ε_2μu, hence (82): ū = (δμ)α(cρ+d) with δ = ε_3 ≡ μ (mod 3).

Meaning. The 'Gaussian' element tσ_∞ + u (attached to the order-4/order-2 point) and the 'Eisenstein' element cρ + d (attached to the order-3 point) are related through f and α_0. Both have norm ±μ^{-1}. The next page observes that this is just the matrix form of the loop relation (56)/(57), namely ε_2U = D and ε_2T = C. Grothendieck then remarks that 'under a false appearance of arithmetic' this is only linear algebra.
errors: Step 3 silently uses μD = 1. Passing from μδ(uC − sD) to δ(−s + μuC) and from μδ(−tC + rD) to δ(r − μtC) requires D = μ^{-1}, i.e. c²+cd+d² = δμ^{-1}. This follows from the loop relation (D = ε_2U together with ε_2μU = 1) but is not stated on this page.
The definition B = δ(ac+bc+bd) (written as 'ac+bc+bd = δB') relies on δ² = 1. This is fine since δ = ±1.
The initial guess (80) is off by the sign δ = ε_3. Grothendieck corrects this himself in the margin and in (82).

ideas.what: Representing the order-3 and order-4 elliptic points by matrix embeddings cρ+d ↔ Ẑ[ρ] (Eisenstein) and tσ_∞+u ↔ Ẑ[i] (Gaussian) inside M_2(Ẑ). Relating them through the GT-type element f, with norms t²+u² and c²+cd+d² both equal (up to sign) to μ^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Abelianized / SL2(Ẑ)-image of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller action; norm conditions in profinite Gaussian and Eisenstein integers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara for GT; Lochak, Schneps and Nakamura for the action on π̂_{1,1} and B_3 → SL2
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the 2- and 3-relations; this explicit matrix computation is not published as far as I know

ideas.what: The bottom rows (t,u) and (c,d) are invariants of the automorphism, determined mod sign, because the ambiguity l_0^n acts by upper unipotent matrices.
ideas.modern_name: Invariance under the unipotent (Borel) ambiguity / double-coset invariants

ideas.what: Verification of relation (82): ū = (δμ)·f^{-1} l_0^{-ν} α_0 (cρ+d), with δ = ε_3 ≡ μ (mod 3).
ideas.modern_name: Matrix form of the 2-cycle/3-cycle (loop) relations of GT in SL2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a sign-tracking linear-algebra verification inside a longer computation. Grothendieck himself notes on the next page that it just re-expresses the known matrix form of the loop relation, and that the 'arithmetic' is really linear algebra. There is no new result or connection beyond the known Gaussian/Eisenstein structure of the elliptic points of SL2.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'est déterminé mod $\underline{l}$ gu[?]' should read 'est déterminé mod signe' ('signe' underlined), continuing '(c,d) … cρ+d' from the previous page; it then reads roughly 'et [word struck] erreur' (probably 'sauf erreur').

Marginal NB: approximately 'NB cette formule n'est valable qu'à un facteur près [?] δ = ε_3, cf (82) plus bas…'. The facteur-près sense is consistent with the image, but the exact wording is uncertain.
Struck passage: reads roughly 'mais pour le moment de reprendre les calculs dans ce sens'; the first word looks like 'mais' rather than 'envie'.
Last line: the factor is written ε_2μt(−st+ru); the meaning (ru − st = 1) is the same.
